macros.name: advanceline
macros.doc: \advanceline takes one argument, an amount that should be added to the current line number; it may be positive or negative.

macros.name: ampersand
macros.doc: If you need to print an & symbol in a stanza, use the \ampersand macro, not \& which will end the stanza.

macros.name: autopar
macros.doc: You can use \autopar to avoid the nuisance of this paragraph markup and still have every paragraph automatically numbered.

macros.name: doendnotes
macros.doc: \doendnotes is the command you use to print one series of endnotes; it takes one argument, the series letter of the note series you want to print.

macros.name: edlabel
macros.doc: The \edlabel command works by writing macros to the LaTeX .aux file.

macros.name: edpageref
macros.doc: If the specified label exists, \edpageref gives its page number.

macros.name: edtabcolsep
macros.doc: The length \edtabcolsep controls the distance between columns.

macros.name: edvertdots
macros.doc: The \edvertdots macro is similar to \edvertline except that it produces a vertical dotted instead of a solid line.

macros.name: endashchar
macros.doc: The \endashchar macro is simply an en-dash from the normal font and is immune to changes in the surrounding font.

macros.name: endlock
macros.doc: You can use \startlock or \endlock in running text to start or end line number locking at the current line.

macros.name: endsub
macros.doc: You insert the \startsub and \endsub commands in your text to turn sublineation on and off.

macros.name: extensionchars
macros.doc: When the package assembles the name of the auxiliary file for a section, it prefixes \extensionchars to the section number.

macros.name: firstlinenum
macros.doc: \firstlinenum specifies the first line that will have a printed number, and \linenumincrement is the difference between succesive numbered lines.

macros.name: flagstanza
macros.doc: Use \flagstanza[len]{text} at the start of a line to put text a distance len before the start of the line.

macros.name: footfootmarkA
macros.doc: This macro typesets the A series marker at the start of the footnote text (where it appears at the foot of the page).

macros.name: footnormalX
macros.doc: \footnormalX is the typical footnote format.

macros.name: footparagraph
macros.doc: The \footparagraph macro sets up everything for one series of footnotes so that they’ll be paragraphed; it takes the series letter as argument.

macros.name: footthreecol
macros.doc: You say \footthreecol{A} to have the A series of footnotes typeset in three columns.

macros.name: foottwocol
macros.doc: You say \foottwocol{A} to have the A series of footnotes typeset in two columns.

macros.name: hangingsymbol
macros.doc: The macro \hangingsymbol is used to insert a symbol on each hanging of verses.

macros.name: interparanoteglue
macros.doc: If you use paragraphed footnotes, the macro \interparanoteglue defines the glue appearing in between footnotes in the paragraph.

macros.name: ledlinenum
macros.doc: \ledlinenum typesets the line (and subline) number.

macros.name: ledlsnotesep
macros.doc: The texts are put a distance \ledlsnotesep (or \ledrsnotesep) into the left (or right) margin.

macros.name: ledlsnotewidth
macros.doc: The left sidenote text is put into a box of width \ledlsnotewidth and the right text into a box of width \ledrsnotewidth.

macros.name: ledplinenumtrue
macros.doc: Following the declaration \ledplinenumtrue critical footnotes will be marked with their line number.

macros.name: ledrsnotesep
macros.doc: The texts are put a distance \ledlsnotesep (or \ledrsnotesep) into the left (or right) margin.

macros.name: ledrsnotewidth
macros.doc: The left sidenote text is put into a box of width \ledlsnotewidth and the right text into a box of width \ledrsnotewidth.

macros.name: leftlinenum
macros.doc: \leftlinenum and \rightlinenum are the macros that are called to print marginal line numbers on a page, for left- and right-hand margins respectively.

macros.name: lemma
macros.doc: The most common use of this command is to abbreviate the lemma that’s printed in the notes.

macros.name: linenumberlist
macros.doc: You can define \linenumberlist to specify a non-uniform distribution of printed line numbers.

macros.name: linenumberstyle
macros.doc: \linenumberstyle and \sublinenumberstyle are user level macros for setting the number represention (\linenumrep and \sublinenumrep) for line and sub-line numbers.

macros.name: linenummargin
macros.doc: You can put the line numbers in the same margin on every page using left or right; or you can use inner or outer to get them in the inner or outer margins.

macros.name: multfootsep
macros.doc: \multfootsep is used as the separator between footnote markers.

macros.name: noendnotes
macros.doc: If you aren’t going to have any endnotes, you can say \noendnotes in your file, before the first \beginnumbering, to suppress the generation of an unneeded .end file.

macros.name: notefontsetup
macros.doc: The font setup defined in \notefontsetup defines the standard fonts for the text of the footnotes.

macros.name: notenumfont
macros.doc: The \notenumfont macro specifies the font used for the line numbers printed in notes.

macros.name: numberlinefalse
macros.doc: Line numbering can be disabled with \numberlinefalse.

macros.name: numberpstarttrue
macros.doc: You can use the command \numberpstarttrue to insert a number on every \pstart.

macros.name: numlabfont
macros.doc: Line numbers are usually printed in a smaller font, and \numlabfont is provided as a standard name for that font.

macros.name: pagelinesep
macros.doc: The page & linenumber combination is written as page\pagelinesep line, where the default definition is \newcommand{\pagelinesep}{-} so that an item on page 3, line 5 will be noted as being at 3-5.

macros.name: pageparbreak
macros.doc: It tries to force TeX into partitioning the current paragraph into two invisibly joined paragraphs with a page break between them.

macros.name: parafootftmsep
macros.doc: You can redefine the \parafootftmsep command to print a separator between each paragraphed footnote (on the same page).

macros.name: rightlinenum
macros.doc: \leftlinenum and \rightlinenum are the macros that are called to print marginal line numbers on a page, for left- and right-hand margins respectively.

macros.name: setline
macros.doc: You can use \setline{⟨num⟩} in running text (i.e., within \pstart...\pend) to set the current visible line-number to a specified positive value.

macros.name: setlinenum
macros.doc: You can use \setlinenum{⟨num⟩} before a \pstart to set the visible line-number to a specified positive value.

macros.name: showlemma
macros.doc: The lemma within the text is printed via \showlemma{lemma}.

macros.name: sidepstartnumtrue
macros.doc: With the \sidepstartnumtrue command, the number of \pstart will be printed in side.

macros.name: skipnumbering
macros.doc: When inserted into a numbered line the macro \skipnumbering causes the numbering of that particular line to be skipped; that is, the line number is unchanged and no line number will be printed.

macros.name: stanza
macros.doc: Use \stanza at the start of a stanza.

macros.name: stanzaindentbase
macros.doc: The indents are integer multiples of the length \stanzaindentbase, whose default value is 20pt.

macros.name: startlock
macros.doc: The \startlock command, used in running text, locks the line number at its current value, until you say \endlock.

macros.name: startsub
macros.doc: \startsub and \endsub turn sub-lineation on and off, by writing appropriate instructions to the line-list file.

macros.name: sublinenumberstyle
macros.doc: \linenumberstyle and \sublinenumberstyle are user level macros for setting the number represention (\linenumrep and \sublinenumrep) for line and sub-line numbers.

macros.name: usingedtext
macros.doc: The declaration \usingedtext must be issued to revert to the default assumption that \edtext will be used.

envs.name: ledgroup
envs.doc: Footnotes in a ledgroup environment are typeset at the end of the environment, as with minipages, but the environment includes normal page breaks.
